item.title: Re: DE-GAW-POI
item.content:encoded:
Sorry for the late reply.

My answer on this and all future edits to add GAW members to the document is this: if there is existing material on this site with said GAW member in it, and they are part of the main GAW group in this article, you can edit it in.

To elaborate: this is very much focused on the main GAW group because I wrote this tale to document and describe the main original group. So it's easier for the Foundation (and therefore me) to not focus on every member from every branch (especially because not every article has been translated). If said GAW member is reasonably part of the main group instead of solely being from another branch, then they can be added.

Also, I will gladly support any other similar dossier-type tales of the group for their respective branches, if there's enough material to work off of, of course. ❤️

item.content:encoded:
kkrule (PoI-6888): 15. Current anomalous abilities are unknown. Youngest member of Gamers Against Weed. The only known anomaly that kkrule has created is SCP-2433. Professes to be straight-edge and is known to frequently play video games more than the other members. Competes in "underground video game tournaments" to make a living; monitoring of eSports tournaments across the United States is underway, but is to be considered low-priority.

Their religion isn't strictly important to the Foundation, but it's heavily relevant to the members of GAW. It influences how they live (and even the anomalies they create) in some way. I also imagine they'd talk about it enough in the server that through piecing together bits of chat logs and snippets, the Foundation would decide to just include it in the dossier anyway.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Personally, I headcanon a lot of realpolitik in the Foundations dealings with people like Jude; on the one hand ideally they would like him to not be running around being a reality bender. On the other, he's really not doing much actual harm, and they've got people trying to unleash Elder Things upon the world and only so many squads of highly trained operatives.

Basically, its the difference between trying to catch Banksy for vandalism and trying to catch a serial killer. Even if they caught Banksy, would anyone really press charges, or would they just give him a stern talking to about filing for permits?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I imagined that, being a coalition of occult organizations to begin with, the GOC probably wants to, y'know, talk with them to see whether they're worth bringing into the fold. If the answer is "absolutely not", then they could probably start escalating.

I also envisioned the main reason the Foundation doesn't just start locking GAW members up being that it could bring on retaliation from the rest of the group. They're quasi-manageable as-is, but what if they got really pissed and started cranking out things with the express purpose of being hard to contain? Nobody wants that.

The events of my own GAW series, incidentally, being the ones that probably informally established this relationship.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Is this standard operating procedure for a threat level Yellow GoI?

I'd imagine so.

Multiple members of this group could be classified as SCPs themselves, in particular Jude who's a full-on reality bender. I don't understand why the Foundation is doing 'catch and release' here.

Because, in my view, the Foundation killing people (even skips) without needing to is cruel and fucked up, especially when said people have hard enough lives as-is. Sure, Jude could be contained and classified as an SCP himself; the Foundation may have considered that and may even adopt that as their plan in the future (AKA, after this dossier was created). But JJ could manage to use his luck to break him out maybe. And even aside from that; it's not exciting narratively.

In-universe, would a group like GAW land on the GOC's radar, and might they take a more 'proactive' approach to dealing with this GoI than the Foundation would?

Possibly? At the moment, I don't think GAW is landing on the GOC's radar in a way to make them want to devote resources to hunt these people down, especially if they're hard to track to begin with.

item.title: Author Post - And I will be alone again tonight my dear.
item.content:encoded:
Thanks to the following (and if I missed anyone, lemme know!):

  • kinchtheknifeblade for looking at so many versions of this and hopefully not being annoyed every time I poked her about it again, as well as helping me with info on many of the characters such as Jude, JJ, Esther, polaricecraps, harmpit, hetcopogg, and gaycopmp4.
  • Communism will win for making me keep working on it even when I thought I was done, and making it better as a result, as well as helping me with various characters such as Jude and harmpit.
  • scarhaver for helping me with bones, JJ, and hetcopogg.
  • Joreth for verifying that all the character attributes I forced onto his characters was good and correct, such as kkrule, TrainerDP, talman_corvett, opossum, tiedyeduck, and DonDeLillo.
  • Monkeysky for coming up with all the ideas for FunkoPopFan1, as well as general critique.
  • doormaker for coming up with all the ideas for fallout_meta.txt, as well as general critique.
  • Ky for making goodpostskitty even better than she already was when pointing out a typo I had, as well as general critique.
  • Aiden Eldritch for tone.
  • ch00bakka for letting me tie CommunismAnarchismNihilism into their SCP-2573.
  • Jekeled, minmin, fenton-st, and DolphinSlugchugger for generally positive feedback.

The idea for a group of interest dossier came to mind when reading eric_h's great Person of Interest - Mr. Dark tale. I wanted to do something similar but for a group of interest. For months, I've been wondering which one to do one on, as I could imagine this sort of format could be real boring for some groups; only a few come to mind that would make it a colorful read. And, well, GAW has been a thing and I've come around from hating it so I decided to do this one.

In writing this, I've come to like the group a lot more (not quite in positive territory, but much closer). I think it's hard to see or imagine, but there are some pretty complex characters here that go deeper than "memes" or what have you. Also; having a group be entirely US-centric and US-focused doesn't feel right, even (and maybe especially) though they're political and mostly are a marginalized group of people. You don't need to live in just America to have your opinions and feelings on such a thing. Hopefully this does a decent job illuminating everything said above. Hopefully you all like it as well!

I added new characters to it and more or less made up my own shit. It's canon. Right now, this document is a snapshot in time and I'm not sure I want this page specifically to either be an open collaboration or updated as stuff gets posted. I'll see what happens and update of my own accord.

2) How do you suppose oppressed reality benders manage to find each other and form a bond and a community?
3) What would the Threat Levels for other Groups of Interest look like?
